items.stem: Old Age Home : Your grandmother has assets of Rs 500,000. One option that she is considering involves an adult residential community for a six-year period beginning in 2020. The model aₙ = 1800n + 64130 describes yearly adult residential community costs n years after 2019. Does your grandmother have enough to pay for the facility?
items.answer: The yearly costs form an arithmetic sequence whose general term is aₙ = 1800n + 64,130, where n is counted from 2019, so n = 1 is the year 2020 and n = 6 is the year 2025. For 2020, a₁ = 1800 × 1 + 64,130 = 65,930. For 2025, a₆ = 1800 × 6 + 64,130 = 74,930. The total cost over the six years is Sₙ = n/2 (a₁ + aₙ), so S₆ = 6/2 (65,930 + 74,930) = 3 × 140,860 = Rs 422,580. Since Rs 422,580 is less than her assets of Rs 500,000, yes — she has enough to pay for the facility for the whole six-year period.
items.ocr: The photograph printed with the question is decorative (an elderly woman with a walking frame), so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
TOWER OF PISA : To prove that objects of different weights fall at the same rate, Galileo dropped two objects with different weights from the Leaning Tower of Pisa in Italy. The objects hit the ground at the same time. When an object is dropped from a tall building, it falls about 16 feet in the first second, 48 feet in the second, and 80 feet in the third second, regardless of its weight.
(i) How many feet would an object fall in the sixth second?
(ii) How many feet would an object fall in the six second?
(iii) How many feet would an object fall in the eight second?
items.answer:
The distances fallen in successive seconds, 16, 48, 80, …, form an AP with a₁ = 16 feet and d = 48 − 16 = 32. The fall during the nᵗʰ second is aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d = 16 + (n − 1)32 = 32n − 16 = 16(2n − 1).
(i) Fall during the 6ᵗʰ second: a₆ = 16(2 × 6 − 1) = 16 × 11 = 176 feet.
(ii) Total fall in 6 seconds: S₆ = 6/2 (a₁ + a₆) = 3(16 + 176) = 3 × 192 = 576 feet.
(iii) Total fall in 8 seconds: S₈ = 8/2 [2 × 16 + (8 − 1) × 32] = 4[32 + 224] = 4 × 256 = 1024 feet.
So the object falls 176 feet during the sixth second, 576 feet in the first six seconds and 1024 feet in the first eight seconds.
items.ocr: The photograph of the Leaning Tower is decorative, so no figure is attached. Two printing slips in the worked solution: the sequence is written '16, 32, 48........' where the stem gives 16, 48, 80, and the common difference is written 'd = 48 − 12 = 32' instead of 48 − 16 = 32; the value d = 32 and the term formula 16(2n − 1) that follow are correct, so the solution stands. The book also labels the third part '(ii)' a second time; it is part (iii). The solution for part (iii) is completed at the top of page 48.

items.stem:
Jessica arranges a display of soup cans as shown in figure.
(i) List the number of cans in the top row, the second row, the third row, and so on, down to the tenth row.
(ii) Write a recursive formula for the terms of the sequence.
(iii) If the cans are to be stacked 47 rows high, how many cans will it take to build the display?
(iv) If Jessica uses six cases (273 cans), how tall can she make the display?
items.answer:
From the display there are 3 cans in the first (top) row, 6 in the second and 9 in the third, so the numbers of cans form an AP with a₁ = 3 and d = 3.
(i) 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30.
(ii) aₙ₊₁ = aₙ + 3, with a₁ = 3.
(iii) Sₙ = n/2 [2a₁ + (n − 1)d], so S₄₇ = 47/2 [2 × 3 + (47 − 1) × 3] = 47/2 [6 + 138] = 47/2 × 144 = 47 × 72 = 3384 cans.
(iv) Put Sₙ = 273: 273 = n/2 [6 + 3(n − 1)], so 546 = n[6 + 3n − 3] = 3n² + 3n, giving 182 = n² + n, i.e. n² + n − 182 = 0. Factorising, (n + 14)(n − 13) = 0, so n = 13 (rejecting n = −14).
Hence she can make the display 13 rows tall with 273 cans.
items.ocr: The stem says 'as shown in figure' and the row counts 3, 6, 9 can only be read off the printed stack, so the display drawing is attached.

items.stem:
Piano : Suppose you practice the piano 45 min on the first day of the semester and increase your practice time by 5 min each day.
(i) How much total time will you devote to practicing during the first 15 days of the semester?
(ii) How much total time will you devote to practicing during the first 35 days of the semester?
items.answer:
Each day is a term of an AP with a₁ = 45 minutes and d = 5 minutes.
(i) For n = 15, Sₙ = n/2 [2a₁ + (n − 1)d] gives S₁₅ = 15/2 [2 × 45 + (15 − 1) × 5] = 15/2 [90 + 70] = 15/2 × 160 = 1200 minutes, that is 20 hours.
(ii) For n = 35, S₃₅ = 35/2 [2 × 45 + (35 − 1) × 5] = 35/2 [90 + 170] = 35/2 × 260 = 4550 minutes, that is 75 hours 50 minutes.
So the practice totals 1200 minutes (20 hours) in the first 15 days and 4550 minutes (75 hours 50 minutes) in the first 35 days.
items.ocr: The book heads the question 'Piono'; written here as 'Piano'. The photograph of a girl at a keyboard is decorative, so no figure is attached. The book also labels the second part of the solution '(i)' a second time; it is part (ii).

items.stem:
RADIO : A radio station is giving away a total of Rs 124,000 in August on promotion. If they increase the amount given away each day by Rs 100,
(i) How much should they give away the first day?
(ii) How much have they give away on the 15th day?
(iii) How much have they give away in 15 day?
items.answer:
The money given away forms an AP with d = 100. August has 31 days and the whole Rs 124,000 is given away in those days, so n = 31 and S₃₁ = 124,000.
(i) Sₙ = n/2 [2a₁ + (n − 1)d] gives 124,000 = 31/2 [2a₁ + 30 × 100], so 8000 = 2a₁ + 3000, hence 2a₁ = 5000 and a₁ = 2500. The station should give away Rs 2,500 on the first day.
(ii) a₁₅ = a₁ + (15 − 1)d = 2500 + 14 × 100 = 2500 + 1400 = Rs 3,900.
(iii) S₁₅ = 15/2 (a₁ + a₁₅) = 15/2 (2500 + 3900) = 15/2 × 6400 = Rs 48,000.
So Rs 2,500 on day one, Rs 3,900 on the fifteenth day and Rs 48,000 over the first fifteen days.
items.ocr: The photograph of a radio presenter is decorative, so no figure is attached. In part (iii) the book writes the subscript as S₃₁ but substitutes n = 15 throughout; the arithmetic it performs is S₁₅ = 15/2 (2500 + 3900) = 48,000, which is what the answer records.

items.stem:
Road Roller : A road roller (sometimes called a roller-compactor, or just roller) is a compactor-type engineering vehicle used to compact soil, gravel, concrete, or asphalt in the construction of roads and foundations. Similar rollers are used also at landfills or in agriculture. Road rollers are frequently referred to as steamrollers, regardless of their method of propulsion.
RCB Machine Pvt Ltd started making road roller 10 year ago. Company increased its production uniformly by fixed number every year. The company produces 800 roller in the 6th year and 1130 roller in the 9th year.
(i) What was the company's production in first year?
(ii) What was the company's production in the 8th year?
(iii) What was the company's total production of the first 6 years?
(iv) What was the increase in the company's production every year?
(v) In which year the company's production was 1350 rollers?
items.answer:
Let a be the production in the first year and d the fixed yearly increase, so the yearly production forms an AP.
Given a₆ = 800: a + 5d = 800 … (1), and a₉ = 1130: a + 8d = 1130 … (2). Subtracting (1) from (2) gives 3d = 330, so d = 110, and then a = 800 − 5 × 110 = 250.
(i) Production in the first year = 250 rollers.
(ii) a₈ = a + 7d = 250 + 7 × 110 = 250 + 770 = 1020 rollers.
(iii) S₆ = 6/2 (a + a₆) = 3(250 + 800) = 3 × 1050 = 3150 rollers.
(iv) The increase every year is d = 110 rollers.
(v) If aₙ = 1350 then 1350 = 250 + (n − 1)110, so (n − 1)110 = 1100 and n − 1 = 10, giving n = 11. The production was 1350 rollers in the 11th year.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems

items.stem: Heavy Penalties : If an air-conditioning system is not completed by the agreed upon date, the contractor pays a penalty of Rs 500 for the first day that it is overdue, Rs 600 for the second day, Rs 700 for the third day, and so on. If the system is completed 10 days late, then what is the total amount of the penalties that the contractor must pay?
items.answer: The daily penalties 500, 600, 700, … form an AP with a₁ = 500, d = 100 and n = 10. Using Sₙ = n/2 [2a₁ + (n − 1)d], S₁₀ = 10/2 [2 × 500 + (10 − 1) × 100] = 5[1000 + 900] = 5 × 1900 = 9500. The contractor must pay a total penalty of Rs 9,500.
